newsitem.title: ALGERIA: Polisario says Morocco king's speech positive.
newsitem.headline: Polisario says Morocco king's speech positive.

text.p: Polisario Front, seeking independence of the Western Sahara from Morocco, said on Saturday it found positive aspects in a recent speech by King Hassan and that it was ready to negotiate a political solution.
In a speech on Wednesday the king for the first time referred in public to direct talks held between Morocco and Polisario to find a solution to the dispute.

"Polisario Front takes note of the positive excerpts of Morocco King's speech. It (expresses) its readiness to start negotiations with the Moroccan party to explore political ways leading to a rapid and integral applying of the U.N. peace plan," the Algerian official APS news agency quoted Polisario as saying.
Polisario guerrillas and Moroccan troops fought for control of Western Sahara for more than 17 years until a 1991 U.N.-sponsored truce.

A U.N. referendum to decide whether the former Spanish colony should be incorporated into Morocco or become independent was originally due in 1992 but has been stalled by endless arguments over who is eligible to take part in the vote.

United Nations Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali recommended on Thursday a six-month renewal of the U.N. operation in Western Sahara. In a report to the Security Council, he referred to "recent indications that the parties are moving forward".
In September, Morocco and Polisario met in Rabat for their first direct talks since 1989. Last month, Morocco freed 66 Polisario prisoners.
